claim: In 1997, when preparing to meet with Iraqi officials, U.S. Ambassador to the United Nations Madeleine Albright decided to make a diplomatic statement by wearing a snake pin.

evidence.quote: Meeting with Iraqi Officials, 1997

When U.S. Ambassador to the United Nations Madeleine Albright criticized Saddam Hussein, his poet-in-residence responded by calling her “an unparalleled serpent.” Shortly thereafter, when preparing to meet with Iraqi officials, Albright decided to make a diplomatic statement by wearing a snake pin (even though she did not like snakes).

notes: Read My Pins exhibit page (National Museum of American Diplomacy, U.S. Department of State).

claim: From the day Albright decided to make a diplomatic statement by wearing a snake pin, pins became part of her diplomatic signature.

evidence.quote: Shortly thereafter, when preparing to meet with Iraqi officials, Albright decided to make a diplomatic statement by wearing a snake pin (even though she did not like snakes).
From that day on, pins became part of her diplomatic signature.
